words: Yes, I think we can have small pictures in Git as sort of, you know, exceptions in GitHub, but everything else should start to move into Vault, right? Because from a performance point of view and a storage point of view, of course, that we now need a website as a place where we can manage all the Vault. Maybe that's actually the Vault's agent. I think we talked about it, right? So we need to make sure we have a good grip of every single public link that we have. But apart from that, yeah, makes sense.
asked: b.abp's two choices on the media rule: (1) the media agents first or every agent; (2) the small link-preview images every site keeps in Git: an exemption, or move them to the vault.
decision: (1) Every agent: images, video and other media start moving into vaults, not Git. (2) Small pictures, such as each site's link-preview images, stay in Git as listed exceptions. (3) The vaults get a home where every vault and every public read link is listed and managed, most likely the vault keeper's site (Site__Agent__Vault-Keeper).

how.rule: b.abp turns its draft (e721c47) into the agent behaviour policy rule; changes under policy/ still need Dinis's merge.
how.exceptions: b.abp proposes the size limit and the list of allowed small pictures; security.b reviews.
how.register: b.vault.keeper keeps the list of vaults and public read links on its site; no vault keys are published there, only read links that are meant to be public.
how.move: Existing media in Git moves to vaults as each keeper next touches its site; nothing is deleted from history by this record.
